title: Outlook for Mac: Purview DLP policy tips with override
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, admin-controlled default, licensing qualifications and override prerequisites are supported. The Purview UI route reaches the correct rule section but should continue to the override option.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Policy tips are part of existing DLP rule handling for Exchange email, with actions defined by the rule.
claims.quote: The conditions and the actions to take are defined in an object called a rule. After you create a DLP policy, it's stored in a central policy store, and then synced to the various content sources, including: Exchange, and from there to Outlook on the web and Outlook

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Override is configured per DLP rule.
claims.quote: The override option is per rule, and it overrides all of the actions in the rule.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: An override overrides all actions in that rule, allowing the sender past a permitted block.
claims.quote: The override option is per rule, and it overrides all of the actions in the rule.

claims.claim: Overriding the most restrictive matching rule also overrides other rules that the content matched.
claims.quote: If the policy tips in the most restrictive rule allow people to override the rule, then overriding this rule also overrides any other rules that the content matched.

claims.claim: Compliance administrator is among the walkthrough's role groups permitted to create and deploy DLP policies.

claims.claim: Security administrator is among the walkthrough's role groups permitted to create and deploy DLP policies.
claims.quote: The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of the following role groups: Compliance administrator; Compliance data administrator; Information Protection; Information Protection Admin; Security administrator

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn requires BlockAccess to be true when NotifyAllowOverride is configured for the override option to appear.
claims.quote: If you set the NotifyAllowOverride action to WithoutJustification or WithJustification or FalsePositives, make sure BlockAccess is set to true and BlockAccessScope has appropriate value.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn also requires an appropriate BlockAccessScope value when NotifyAllowOverride is configured.
claims.quote: If you set the NotifyAllowOverride action to WithoutJustification or WithJustification or FalsePositives, make sure BlockAccess is set to true and BlockAccessScope has appropriate value.

claims.claim: Without those prerequisites, a policy tip can appear without an option to override the email with justification.
claims.quote: Otherwise, the policy tip comes up but the user doesn't find an option to override the email with justification.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The Purview route through DLP Policies, the Custom policy wizard, Exchange email and Create rule reaches User notifications and Policy tips for configuring rule override.
claims.quote: Set the User notifications toggle to On. Select Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only). If already selected, uncheck the Allow override from M365 services option.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the rendered table to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom > Full directory > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > Policy tips > Allow override from M365 services'. The cited walkthrough documents this option; select it when override is intended rather than following the walkthrough's no-override example.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -NotifyAllowOverride WithJustification modifies the named rule to allow overrides with justification.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the DLP rule that you want to modify. The NotifyAllowOverride parameter specifies the notification override options when the conditions of the rule are met. WithJustification: Allows overrides with justification.

claims.claim: Enabling the tip UI and configuring a rule's override are separate controls in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center and Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: For each rule in a DLP policy, you can configure policy tips to: Notify the person that the content conflicts with a DLP policy. Allow the person to override the DLP policy. The override option is per rule
